added_claim_errors: "$1,220+ evaporates on January 1" incorrectly fixes forfeiture before the run-out deadline; timely claims for eligible prior-year expenses still count.
"Many offer neither" adds an unsupported claim about plan prevalence.
"Usually ~90 days" adds an unverified typical run-out deadline; the actual deadline is plan-specific.
"All $1,900 stays usable, but only through March 15" treats the maximum grace period as the actual period; plans may provide less time.
"Confirm the office will charge before the 15th" uses the payment date instead of the date care is provided.
Moving dental work into December "uses 100% of the money" assumes an unspecified dental cost.
"Spending $1,500 ... to save $680" misstates the spend-down tradeoff: eligible spending consumes the otherwise forfeitable balance, rather than merely saving the carryover.
"Carried into next year (best case) ~$680" overlooks the grace-period possibility of using all $1,900, despite acknowledging it later.
"Carryover only happens if you're ... still enrolled" presents a potentially plan-specific enrollment condition as universal.
"If you change jobs, the whole balance ... is gone" omits the COBRA exception and is overly absolute.
"Usually have until March–April" adds an unverified typical filing deadline; the actual run-out deadline is plan-specific.

reasons: A gives the clearer opening correction and more accurate carryover explanation; independently recomputing $1,900 − $680 confirms $1,220. B adds unsupported universal enrollment and job-change restrictions and misleadingly labels $680 the best case. Both omit the 2027 election strategy and explicit warning against prepaying March dental work; A additionally confuses charging with receiving care and overstates the grace-period endpoint. Added claims were assessed against the packet and general knowledge, without external verification.
